poppi.ig:
They asked for $400K. Six years later, PepsiCo agreed to pay $1.95B.

Mother Beverage (now Poppi) asked $400K for 10%, a $4M valuation. Kevin called it insane. Only guest Shark Rohan Oza offered: same $400K, for 25%. They took it, at a $1.6M valuation.

In 2025 PepsiCo bought Poppi for $1.95B. PepsiCo said $300M of that was expected tax benefits, so the net price was $1.65B.

Don't just fight the valuation. Price the partner. And every headline number has a net number underneath it.

Would you have taken 25% from the right partner over 10% from nobody? Yes or no?

moki.ig:
A $3M licensing deal. Then a $3M offer for the whole company.

Moki Doorstep asked $150K for 5%. On air, the founder said a licensing deal guaranteed $3M over seven years plus a 12.5% royalty. Daymond offered $450K for 20%, then $3M for 100%. They accepted on the spot.

What happened after the cameras stopped? Public reports conflict, so we won't guess. The math holds either way: at a 10% discount rate (illustrative), $3M paid over 7 years is worth about $2.1M today.

Price a royalty stream in today's dollars. A guarantee paid over years is not cash in hand.

Equity is the most expensive money you can raise. Get distribution without selling ownership when you can.
